{{Character|name=Kaeden Brewmane|image=[[File:Kaeden_'Brewmane'_Ironwill_2.png]]|affiliation=Ironwill Clan, Ironforge, The Alliance|occupation=Rune Priest, Priest, Physician|birthPlace=Loch Modan|race=Dwarf|gender=Male|height=132 cm {{!}} 4'3"|weight=72 kg {{!}} 159 lbs|eyes=Blue|hair=Gray|birthDate=-209 (236 Years Old)|status=Alive}}
''Rendering priestly service tae' any ah'n all in need, he'll be sure tae' interest ya'n a pint just like th' good Father orders.''
== Physical Appearance == Kaeden looks to be a stout, and portly dwarf of middling age and height. His eyes are kind, adding to a genial visage that’s flanked by two full rosy cheeks. Donned in priestly vestments, the garment harbors visible stains which paint a history of misplaced ale. His better half- the beard, appears immaculately cared for having been combed down neatly into a luscious center-mass and banded together just inches before the ends would meet. Alongside of which, two smaller clasps rest in a similar manner. The ensemble strikes a certain quality in the otherwise unkempt priest. == Character Backstory == Kaeden Brewmane was born the last son of Clan Brewmane within Khaz Modan’s eastern frontier- the temperate, hilly region of Loch Modan. His family maintained a small, yet profitable brewery that was enough to support his kin- as well as the ever-parched dwarves set to work within nearby archaeological digsites. In his youth, Kaeden had learned mundane methods of first-aid from the local guardsmen patrol, and found purpose in helping those in need within surrounding communities. From setting splints for broken bones suffered in digsite accidents to wrapping and treating wounds sustained from encounters with local wildlife- Kaeden garnered a local reputation that allowed for a meager, though honest source of income to which he was grateful for. Years had passed, and Kaeden had begun to develop a keen sense of longing to advance his knowledge in the arts of healing; a longing that was satiated within the Great Halls of Ironforge. Having spent the time required within Ironforge to advance his abilities- Kaeden poised himself ready to utilize these newfound skills and give back to the ones who gave him this purpose in life; by joining the Medical Corps of Ironforge’s Armies and assisting those within the frontier reaches of Khaz Modan just like the guardsmen before him.[[File:Kaeden Bruuk Resize.png|thumb|Kaeden, seen within Bruuk's Corner waving the man down for a Flagon of Ale.]]Time flowed swiftly, as each case would prove to be a novel experience which cumulatively instilled mastery over his craft. Having seen the extent of the frontier and the previously unknown dangers within, Kaeden’s worldview expanded considerably; a sense of scale now fully developed within the mind of the dwarf. Many decades had passed by now, and the drums of war soon emerged across Khaz Modan- the Second War had begun. Unbeknownst to Clan Brewmane- who were still prospering within the frontiers of Loch Modan, Khaz Modan would soon be the target of the Orcish Horde. Seeking the rich variety of valuable metal ores and oil- in addition to the dwarves’ mighty forges- before continuing on, well-equipped to launch their assault on Lordaeron soon afterwards. As the Invasion of Khaz Modan progressed, the Dwarves of Ironforge soon retreated back within their Great Halls (as did the Gnomes within Gnomeregan), readying themselves to outlast the enfolding siege. Kaeden was among those within the Great Halls assisting the wounded- and counting every dead. Seeing the Dwarves as the greater threat between the two races, the Armies commanded by Ogrim Doomhammer focused their attentions on Ironforge. The dwarves, now recognizing the severity of their circumstances, realized this would be their last stand and adopted a stoic sense of endurance in the face of insurmountable adversity. Prepared to die fighting, their fury unrivaled. Of course- even a dwarven medic would die fighting to the last for the sake of their Kingdom’s survival. Kaeden was ready in-arms despite his lack of martial training; ready to give back for every counted dead. ''“How dare they threaten our ancestral home- our very existence?”'' he’d thought. In these moments of internal-strife, a fury began to swell within. Much like the waters of The Loch held beyond the Stonewrought Dam- a rising tide of indignant rage threatened to give way and burst out against the enemy. In spite of that, another voice grew from within- one of reason and purpose; a voice of faith. Listening further, Kaeden grasped onto this voice which felt so distant- yet exuded familiarity as if it were present the whole time. Simultaneously, the adjacent fury threatening to breach forth moments before began to diminish in kind. Stemming from the faith which Kaeden now held cradled within- a veil of warmth began to enshroud his inner being. Falling upon his shoulders and enveloping much like the embrace of his own mother. Laced with nostalgia reminiscent of better days- a feeling of peace now sprouting from within. Kaeden stepped back, growing reassured in his role. Setting forth with a focused dedication to save anymore wounded he could- this was where he was most impactful. Not on the frontlines amongst the others- not yet. Certainly not while droves of wounded soldiers lay writhing in pain; not when he could ease their suffering. His hands moved with a skilled assurance which, when observed by others, spoke of experience acquired through decades of practice. As he worked, the bandages and thread which mended flesh to bone began to emanate a warmth of their own; a radiating luminescence which was noted by onlookers. Kaeden spoke no words- no response but for his own genial visage, giving reassurance all the same.
''It was within these Great Halls that Kaeden Brewmane's faith in the Light was founded, and his purpose grew in bounds with that faith.''
Every resource was mobilized, and nearly the entire population took up arms to resist the siege. Every man, woman, and child within Ironforge was ready to die for the sake of their kin that day. As the siege intensified, the death toll proved horrendous for the orcs; for every dwarf that fell- ten orcs were felled in turn. In time, the cost grew so great that Doomhammer called off the siege. At the same time- the Orcish Horde were met with similar results when attempting an assault on Gnomeregan, and both sieges were ultimately called off. The cities had proven too costly in both time and manpower, but their short-term goals were still met nevertheless. The bountiful resources of Khaz Modan were taken, and horde smiths quickly got to work while the Bleeding Hollow Clan kept watch on both sides- keeping both dwarf and gnome contained for the duration of the war. The days to follow were grim and bloody for those wayward refugees seeking to escape from the encroaching Horde, and Clan Brewmane was no exception to this. The Loch was swiftly overrun by the conflict and bloodshed which ensued; the Clan's homestead and brewery razed to the ground by orcish raiding parties. Years passed, and as the war progressed with the emergence of the newly formed Alliance- the Orcish Horde were pushed back in full-retreat. The Alliance was advancing to liberate Khaz Modan beyond the Thandol Span- and so they did. With the last vestige of Bleeding Hollow Clan orcs now defeated at their doors, the Dwarves of Ironforge and the Gnomes of Gnomeregan emerged from their cities for the first time in years. Celebrating the lifting of the siege, both the dwarves and gnomes eagerly joined the Alliance. Hunting parties scoured the lands soon after, rooting out any remaining presence of enemy occupation. The pursuit resumed and the Horde were routed at Blackrock- the Dark Portal destroyed soon after, of which we all know. The Alliance was victorious, yet the cost had been high. Too high for some. [[File:Broken Horde Ballista.png|thumb|A broken Horde ballista laying alongside Loch Modan's main highway. ]] Kaeden had spent many months after the war searching for his kin to no avail. It was clear that the Orcish Horde were too swift; the liberation of Khaz Modan too late. Clan Brewmane was annihilated during the time of the Second War, like many others slain beside them. To this day, broken Horde catapults and billistae can be seen strewn about the lands of Loch Modan. A mute and somber means of evidence to the region’s brief- though bloody, and sorrowfull history. '''Kael'thas Sunstrider''' is the former prince of the [[High elf|high elven]] kingdom of [[Quel'Thalas (kingdom)|Quel'Thalas]] and the current leader of the [[Blood elf|blood elves]]. Considered a traitor for allying himself with the naga and with the also considered traitor [[Illidan Stormrage]], he is currently in [[Outland]] allied with the [[Illidari]] in the hope of finding some way to save his people from the magical addiction that afflicts them, after the fall of Quel'Thalas and the destruction of the [[Sunwell]]. ==Background== Kael'thas spent most of his time in [[Dalaran]], where he was a member of [[Council of Dalaran|the Six]], a secretive council that very few knew the existence of; as a high elf and the relationships that humans and elves had formed since the Troll Wars, he had earned such a privilege to be part of the government of a city shared between humans and high elves. ===Third War=== Kael'thas was in Dalaran when the Scourge swept through Quel'Thalas, killing most of the high elves, corrupting the Sunwell and killing Kael'thas' father, King [[Anasterian Sunstrider|Anasterian]]. Upon hearing of the attack, Kael'thas hurried back to Quel'Thalas only to find such a sight. He immediately gathered the surviving high elves and, in honor of those who had died, renamed them to the blood elves. With a regiment of blood elves, Kael left for Lordaeron to help the [[Alliance Remnants|remnants of the Alliance]] that was still fighting against the Scourge, but Grand Marshal [[Othmar Garithos]], with a strong hatred towards the elves, sent them on suicide missions. After repeatedly allying against the Scourge to ensure the elves' survival with [[Lady Vashj]] and her naga, whom the Grand Marshal distrusted for being inhuman, Lord Garithos sentenced Kael'thas to death after learning of his second alliance with the naga. However, Kael'thas managed to escape from the dungeons of Dalaran with the aid of Lady Vashj before he could be executed. After this, Kael allied himself with Illidan Stormrage in his attempt to conquer Outland, and subsequently, the Frozen Throne. Upon being defeated in the latter, Kael took Illidan and along with Lady Vashj and several blood elves and returned to Outland, where they remain to this day. It is because of these alliances that Kael'thas has been branded a traitor and a coward by his people. However, not all the blood elves returned to Outland; a portion of Kael'thas' forces remained on Azeroth and continued to occupy the mountain stronghold of [[Felstrider Retreat]] in the [[Thalassian Highlands]], led by Kael'thas' distant cousin [[Eldin Sunstrider|Eldin]]. ===Mysteries of Azeroth=== Kael'thas remains in Outland, allied with the [[Illidari]], seeking a way to cure the addiction of those he considers his people, both the high elves and the blood elves. Many consider him dead, since they saw how the promise of his return faded over time, and with the worrying news of his alliances with the naga and with the demon hunters, he is maintained as a traitor among the high elves of the [[Silvermoon Remnant]]. Kael keeps an eye on the elves of [[Alah'Thalas]] through the Felstrider Retreat and by maintaining direct communication with a member of the new [[Regency Council]], [[Grand Magister Rommath]], who still holds faith in his prince and his quest to find a cure for the elves' magical addiction. ==Quotes== ;Greeting * I'm waiting. * I feel edgy. * My people must be avenged. ;Farewell * Outstanding. * My pleasure. ;Pissed * Nothing of my homeland remains, but ash and sorrow. * My hunger for magic is clouding my judgment! * All I feel is hate and rage. * The Alliance has failed my people. {{DEFAULTSORT:Sunstrider, Kael'thas}} [[Category:High elf characters]] [[Category:Blood elf characters]] [[Category:Aristocrats]] [[Category:Dalaran (kingdom)]] [[Category:Illidari]]

== Khasya Tanarian ==
{{Character|name=Khasya Tanarian|image=Khasya-portrait.png|faction=Chaotic Neutral|affiliation=None|faffiliation=Steamwheedle Cartel|occupation=Sorceress|status=Adventurer|birthPlace=Tanaris|birthDate=9 ADP|race=Human|gender=Female|eyes=Black|hair=Black}}
Khasya is a wandering sorceress seeking fortune and pleasure throughout Azeroth. Her talents in evocation and divination spells are impressive, but she doesn't have the arrogance like the mages of Dalaran, which makes it easy for people to get along with her.

==== '''Occupations''' ====
Khasya is not only a natural spellcaster, but has also received private magic training since childhood. Her spellcasting abilities have been tested in Azeroth's harshest environments, which proven her worth countless times.

Before becoming a freelance adventurer, Khasya was employed by the Gadgetzan Water Company, a subsidiary of the Steamwheedle Cartel. Khasya has creatively used reactions between various elements to determine the location of water veins, plays a role in the discovery of many underground water sources in the desert.

==== '''Looks''' ====
Khasya has the exotic appearance of Southsea people. Her eyes were as dark as black pearl, and her hair as silky and dark as nightsaber fur. Khasya's skin is bronzed, smooth and hydrated. Her figure is not plump, but she has attractive curves.

Khasya prefers simple, breathable clothing and does not like to wrap herself too tightly. She likes gold jewelry, the most obvious of which are the two gold bracelets on her right wrist. When she casts a spell, they collide and make crisp sound.

Khasya smokes sungrass and licorice from a long pipe, it was such a long-standing habit that it made her voice slightly rapsy.

==== '''Personality''' ====
Khasya is witty, foxy and sarcastic, even acquaintances have trouble telling which of her words are serious. But she believed it effectively weeded out the fribbles and idiots around her. 

Khasya is as free and searing as the desert wind, and it is hard to be tied down by any rules. However, she is no more interested in breaking the law than she is in understanding its authority, so whenever she arrived in a new land, she didn't waste much time in jail. Khasya doesn't like conflict, but is quite vengeful. In battle, Khasya is confident and cunning, with no sense of honor.
[[File:Khasya-FM.png|left|thumb|425x425px|Although Khasya is classified as a hydromancer by the Gadgetzan Water Co., fire is her true symbol.]]



Khasya has a great enthusiasm for things or people that interest her, although it may be short-lived like candle light, the passion is always like fire - takes all and gives all. This foehn of attraction had attracted many people to her, a few are capable enough to be her companions, fewer of them interested her, and even fewer could have kept her interested after the bonfire had gone out. Although risks always follow this lifestyle, Khasya has her own way out of these messes. Some people think she is emotionally selfish.

Khasya is a money-obsessed person who lacks long-term vision. Nothing seems to impress her except material things. But she is not a miser. After making some money, she often shares enjoyments generously with her companions, and then quickly becomes poor again, and then looks for the next opportunity to make a fortune, and the cycle starts again. 

== Backstory ==
Khasya may have been the first human she knew born on Tanaris. In the year she was born, even the pirates from the Southsea had not yet landed on this dry land.

It all starts with the story of Khasya's parents, and it may not be credible - she has a father who only be honesty when chanting spells and a mother who doesn't know what honesty is, but in any case, this is the only way she knows her origins...Well, she doesn't really care about that too.

Khasya's father is said to be a sorcerer from Dalaran. He took part in the second war, but was unhappy with the authorities because he was forced to hand over some valuable artifacts he had looted from horde warlocks. So in 8 ADP he organized a group of rogue mages to heist the vault of Dalaran. They didn't get the loot they were looking for, but the fact that Teron Gorefiend stole the Eye of Dalaran at the very same night made the heist team a suspect for high treason. Khasya's father escaped from Dalaran overnight and boarded an owler ship heading south.

The ship's destination was originally Booty Bay, but off Khaz Modan they were attacked by Southsea pirates, and as if that wasn't enough, the pirate ship was followed by Dragonmaw riders, and the red dragons then attacked the two tied-up ships. In the chaos of the fire, Khasya's father tried to teleport to escape, but at this time, a she-pirate swooped at him and disrupted his chanting. As a result, the two entangled morons were teleported to the desert of Tanaris. No body knows how they walked from the center of the desert to Steamwheedle Port alive. According to their saying, "then poff, here you are".

As a rare talent of the Steamwheedle Cartel, Khasya's father quickly gained a place in Gadgetzan, as for mother, she robbed the midwife as soon as she could jumped off the delivery bed. 

All in all, Khasya grew up in the goblin community, inherited her spellcasting talent from her father, and her appearance is almost exactly the same as her mother. Growing up, Khasya's father taught her everything he had learned throughout his life in Dalaran; her mother taught her how to survive in a sinister world and the cream of Southsea philosophy. 

The successful family education made Khasya to throw a fireball into the face of a strange big man at the age of 11 , that was the first time she saw anyone bigger than goblins or her parents at the shore - This year, the wastewanders landed on the coast of Tanaris.

As Khasya grew up, she began to take her father's place in the Gadgetzan Water Company. In fact, long before Khasya grew up, she had been deep into the desert several times with goblin exploration teams. She soon proved that she was more talented than her father. With her help, the company discovered more water sources in the desert and set up pumping stations, so that the desert could support a larger population. Khasya was also inevitably involved in many battles with beasts, Qiraji, wastewanders, and sand trolls. All this made her stronger and made her rich at a young age.

With the end of the Third War, the rise of the Alliance and the Horde in Kalimdor made trade in the south active again. Many outsiders appeared in Gadgetzan, bringing news to Khasya about the wider world. Taking this as an opportunity, Khasya ended her career of working for goblins, became an adventurer, and began to learn the pleasure that the whole world could bring her.

{{Alliance}}{{RaceIcon|NightElf|Male}} [[Fandral Staghelm]] | languages = Orcish, Taur-ahe, Troll, Darnassian, Goblin | loc = Western Azeroth|faffiliation=}} '''Kalimdor''' [[International Phonetic Alphabet|[ˈkælɪmdɔɹ]]] ([[Darnassian]] for '''land of eternal starlight''') is one of the two main continents of [[Azeroth]]. It is located to the west of the [[Eastern Kingdoms]]. The [[Great Sea]] lies in between the continents. Kalimdor is home to the [[Night elf|night elves]], [[Orc|orcs]], [[tauren]] and [[Troll|trolls]]. Other races present include the [[Ogre|ogres]], [[centaur]], [[naga]], [[demons]], and other, more minor races. Kalimdor was primarily the domain of the night elves in the ten thousand years between the [[War of the Ancients]] and the [[Battle of Mount Hyjal]]. In the years since the battle, night elf dominion has given way as the tauren adopted a more centralized system and accepted their allies, the orcs and the trolls into their midst. Now, however, the continent is a politically divided one, the Horde have established strong control in the central and eastern areas while the night elves, preserve footholds in northwestern areas. [[File:WorldMap-Kalimdor.jpg|350px|thumb|In-game map of Kalimdor.]] ==History== === After the War of the Ancients === {| class="fandom-table" | |This section is '''a [[lore]] stub'''. |} After the [[Highborne]]'s departure, the remaining night elves deliberately withdrew from the rest of the world. A veil of mist descended upon their entire continent, shrouding its presence from passing sailors. The knowledge of Kalimdor survived in some old [[human]] legends, but without details about its history or whereabouts, merely that the land was broken and set beneath the waves during the [[Great Sundering|Sundering of the World]]. ===Second War=== After their defeat at the hands of Doomhammer's Horde on the [[Broken Isles]], surviving members of the [[Twilight's Hammer]] sailed west to the mysterious continent of Kalimdor, drawn in by the whispers of the [[Old Gods]]. ===Third War=== {| class="fandom-table" | |This section is '''a [[lore]] stub'''. |} As the [[Third War]] started, Kalimdor was still considered a mere legend among most humans, with people such as the [[Kirin Tor]] ambassador to [[Terenas Menethil II|King Terenas]]' court not believing in its existence. A few heeded [[Medivh]]'s warning however and traveled west, such as [[Thrall]]'s new [[Horde]] and [[Jaina Proudmoore]]'s [[Human Expedition|expedition]]. ==Geography== Kalimdor has a huge variety of both animal and plant life. Within this continent, you will find almost every land type; from the ice cold plains of [[Winterspring]] in the north, to the hot desert of [[Tanaris]] in the south. The mystical woods of [[Ashenvale]], the dry, rocky [[Thousand Needles]], the tropical, lush jungle of [[Feralas]] — this continent has it all. To the north the landscape is primarily coated in thick alpine woodland, typical in areas such as [[Ashenvale]]. Central Kalimdor, home to the horde, is far more rugged and barren, save for the safety of Mulgore. In the south, desert areas dominate the terrain; however, nestled between these bleak landscapes are realms of beauty and wonder such as the thriving tropical regions of [[Feralas]] and [[Un'Goro Crater]]. ===Regions=== Kalimdor has been shown to be divided into three great regions or continents: * [[Northern Kalimdor]] * [[Central Kalimdor]] * [[Southern Kalimdor]] Kalimdor is further divided into the following regions: *[[File:Expansion_logo_mysteriesofazeroth.png|40px]] {{Horde}} [[Blackstone Island]] (1 - At first, Khadgar believed Medivh to be nothing more than he appeared to be, a kindly, old, if slightly eccentric wizard, but it wasn't long before he began to sense something was drastically wrong with his master. Though he never suspected that Medivh was actually being controlled by [[Sargeras]], the Dark Titan, he became suspicious of his master's actions and motives. Eventually, he unraveled Medivh's plot to open a portal between Azeroth and Draenor after meeting a Horde emmisary, the half-orc assassin [[Garona]]. Knowing it was already too late to stop the [[Dark Portal]] from opening further, Khadgar and Garona rushed to King [[Llane Wrynn]] of [[Stormwind (kingdom)|Azeroth]] for help. The pair, along with Lord [[Anduin Lothar]] and a group of soldiers returned to Karazhan to find Medivh in psychic link with the orc warlock [[Gul'dan]]. Khadgar managed to defeat Medivh in magical combat, banishing both his soul, and that of Sargeras who was controlling him. Medivh himself was slain by Lothar.''The Last Guardian'' Following Medivh's death and the fall of Stormwind to the orcs, Khadgar fled north with Lord Lothar and the rest of the refugees to Lordaeron. He spent the [[Second War]] fighting with the [[Alliance of Lordaeron]], all the while studying Medivh's spells and the nature of the Dark Portal. When the tide of the war turned and the Alliance managed to push the Horde back to the Portal itself, Khadgar attempted to destroy the Dark Portal, effectively severing the link between Azeroth and Draenor. The rift between worlds remained, however. To guard against a second attack from Draenor, Khadgar oversaw the construction of [[Nethergarde Keep]] in the Black Morass. In the aftermath of the Second War, the Kirin Tor dispatched an assembly of mages to search Karazhan and seize all items of import for the purposes of research.[[Archmage Angela Dosantos#Gossip about Atiesh]] The [[Council of Six]] approached Khadgar for aid in venturing into the tower and retrieving those dangerous relics left behind during the chaos of Anduin Lothar's assault on Karazhan. With the aid of Archmage [[Vandol]], sent by Archmage [[Antonidas]], he secured some of Medivh's artifacts to bring them to Dalaran.[[Khadgar's Journal]] Khadgar's fears would be validated only a year after Nethergarde's completion, when the portal opened again, and orc forces began pouring out, striking strategically to steal powerful artifacts. Fearing a second invasion, Khadgar led an [[Alliance Expedition]] to the orc homeworld, where he quickly discovered that the situation was even worse than he had feared. The orcs, under the leadership of the shaman [[Ner'zhul]], were planning on opening doorways to new worlds for the Horde to plunder. Unable to stop Ner'zhul from opening his portals, and unable to contain the terrible energies they unleashed, the archmage used Medivh's spellbook to close the Dark Portal from the other side, thereby shielding Azeroth from the final cataclysm of Draenor's destruction. '''Kargath Bladefist''' was the chieftain of the [[Shattered Hand clan]]. A razor-sharp scythe setting in place of his severed left hand, Kargath was always willing to engage in frenzied combat. His ruthless tactics and single-mindedness have earned him the Chieftainship of the feared Shattered Hand clan. Like [[Grommash Hellscream|Hellscream]], Kargath waited only for the time his clan cold be unleashed upon the unsuspecting humans to engage in massive bloodshed.

==History==
The Shattered Hand had stayed in Draenor when the orcs first crossed the Dark Portal and were spared the defeat that ended the Second War. Under Kargath, the Shattered Hand and the [[Thunderlord clan]] lent their forces to [[Dentarg]] to reclaim the [[Skull of Gul'dan]] from a captain of the [[Bonechewer clan]].<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Skull_of_Gul%27dan_(WC2_Orc) The Skull of Gul'dan (WC2 Orc)]</ref> Kargath later led a force of Shattered Hand orcs into Azeroth.<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Beyond_the_Dark_Portal_(WC2_Human) Beyond the Dark Portal (WC2 Human)]</ref> Kargath's Shattered Hand army defended the Azerothian side of the Dark Portal during the last days of the Invasion of Draenor, and they were left stranded with their chieftain after Ner'zhul abandoned them and the Portal was destroyed by the Alliance.<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Dark_Portal_(WC2_Orc) The Dark Portal (WC2 Orc)]</ref>

The Shattered Hand's status during the interim period between the destruction of the Dark Portal and the fall of the internment camps is unknown; of Kargath's contemporaries, [[Kilrogg Deadeye|Kilrogg]] of the [[Bleeding Hollow clan|Bleeding Hollow]] was captured along with his clan, while [[Grom Hellscream]] of the [[Warsong clan]] continued to evade the Alliance.<ref>''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'' Game Manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#Day_of_the_Dragon Orcish History]'', Day of the Dragon</ref> Supported by many of the veteran chieftains, [[Thrall]] ultimately succeeded in revitalizing the Horde and giving his people a new spiritual identity.<ref name="ThrallsTale">''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'' Game Manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#Thrall's_Tale Orcish History]'', Thrall's Tale</ref>

The Shattered Hand still exists, making their home in the [[Cleft of Shadow]], located in the orcish capital of [[Orgrimmar]].

==Trivia==

The air of [[Deadwind Pass]] is harsh and unforgiving. I remember the place before [[First War|the Orcish invasion]] - lush and green, with a pleasant breeze passing from [[Grand Hamlet]]. Nothing of that remains, however. Only the destruction wrought by my master and his sins.
----
The [[Council of Six]] asked me for assistance in retrieving dangerous relics left behind during the chaos of [[Anduin Lothar|Lothar]]'s assault on [[Karazhan]]. I don't like to return to this place full of memories, good and bad. Reliving the past aches my heart, just as my aged body is aching at the strain of my journey. At least I have [[Vandol]] with me, although he isn't eager to return here either. [[Antonidas]] tasked him with safekeeping the artifacts I retrieve. While I could've done so too, I trust the archmage's judgement.
----
Tethered spirits roam the empty halls, some familiar, some unknown. I even faintly heard the voice of Castellan [[Moroes]], yet I couldn't see him. His humor was a ray of sunshine during my rigid studies with the master. Hopefully his soul can find respite at some point in time.
----
The upper reaches were locked, but luckily I still have a key for them in my possession. The atmosphere is different, more hostile. I have to proceed with caution, lest I get surprised by horrors left behind.
----
Master's library is still mostly intact. I am astonished how it survived Karazhan's desolation. Should I ever get the time and a few fellow mages from the Kirin Tor with me, bringing his knowledge to Dalaran would be a valuable boon to the Council and its students.
----
I came across an enigmatic contraption lying between the hefty tomes. It's made from arcanite, enchanted with a powerful ward and in immaculate condition. There is no doubt in my mind that this was of importance for the master, my heart tells me so. Judging from its appearance, I'd say it is a sort of clasp for a gemstone.
----
I managed to collect a few more of Medivh's artifacts. This place is still cursed, and I have to make haste to exit it unharmed. Vandol awaits me outside in hiding, so we may return safely back to Dalaran. It is strange to travel with one of Master's close friends, after all that has happened. Still, we share each other's company, as I can relate to him, as much as he can relate to me.
----
Another being is close, a hostile one. For a second its presence felt identical to the master's, but that quickly changed - not that it would've been possible either way. An aura of a bygone time, is how I would describe it. Regardless, I will remain cautious on my way-

<The journal abruptly ends. Luckily you know that this wasn't the end of Khadgar.>

For years he held control of the Plaguelands and fought against the forces of the [[Scarlet Crusade]], the [[Argent Dawn]], the [[Alliance]], and the [[Horde]] until his defeat at the hands of adventurers. ==Biography== ===The Call of the Lich King=== Kel'Thuzad was one of the greatest Archmagi of [[Dalaran (kingdom)|Dalaran]]. He was one of the members of the [[Kirin Tor]] and was once a dear friend of the Archmage [[Antonidas]]. However, his lust to delve into the dark arts of necromancy made him an outcast amongst his fellow wizards.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#Kel'Thuzad Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos manual#Kel'Thuzad] There were a handful of powerful individuals, scattered across the world, who heard the Lich King's mental summons from Northrend. Most notable of them was the Archmage Kel'Thuzad, of the magical nation of [[Dalaran (kingdom)|Dalaran]]. Kel'Thuzad, one of the senior members of the [[Kirin Tor]] — Dalaran's ruling council — had been considered a maverick for years due to his insistence on studying the forbidden arts of necromancy. Driven to learn all he could of the magical world and its shadowy wonders, he was frustrated by what he saw as his peers' outmoded and unimaginative precepts. Upon hearing the powerful summons from Northrend, the Archmage bent all of his considerable will to communing with the mysterious voice. Convinced that the Kirin Tor was too squeamish to seize the power and knowledge inherent in the dark arts, he vowed to learn what he could from the immensely powerful Lich King. At some point prior to the Third War, Antonidas learned that Kel'Thuzad had been experimenting with necromancy by reanimating dead rats. Fearing for the safety and reputation of Dalaran, Antonidas had Kel'Thuzad's properties searched, and all items tainted by dark magic were confiscated and destroyed. Antonidas warned Kel'Thuzad that he would be stripped of his rank and holdings and exiled from both Dalaran and Lordaeron, if he did not abandon his "madness".''[[Road to Damnation]]'' Forsaking his fortune and prestigious political standing, Kel'Thuzad abandoned the ways of the Kirin Tor and left Dalaran forever. Prodded by the Lich King's persistent voice in his mind, he sold his vast holdings and stored away his fortunes. Travelling alone over many leagues of both land and sea, he finally reached the frozen shores of Northrend. Intent on reaching Icecrown and offering his services to the Lich King, the Archmage passed through the ravaged, war-torn ruins of [[Azjol-Nerub]]. Kel'Thuzad saw firsthand the scope and ferocity of [[Ner'zhul]]'s power. He began to believe that allying himself with the mysterious Lich King would not only be wise, but potentially fruitful. Kel'Thuzad met with [[Anub'arak]], who told him of all the power he could wield. Frightened by the horrors that he saw in Naxxramas, Kel'Thuzad teleported out and tried to escape. Unfortunately, he was surrounded by wraiths and was brought back inside. After long months of trekking through the harsh arctic wastelands, Kel'Thuzad finally reached the dark glacier of [[Icecrown]]. He boldly approached Ner'zhul's dark citadel and was shocked when the silent undead guardsmen let him pass as though he was expected. Kel'Thuzad descended deep into the cold earth and found his way down to the bottom of the glacier. There, in the endless cavern of ice and shadows, he prostrated himself before the Frozen Throne and offered his soul to the dark lord of the dead. To help the Archmage accomplish his mission, Ner'zhul left Kel'Thuzad's humanity intact. The aged, yet still charismatic wizard was charged with using his powers of illusion and persuasion to lull the downtrodden, disenfranchised masses of Lordaeron into a confidence. Once he had their attention, he would offer them a new vision of what society could be – and a new figurehead to call their king. ===The Cult of the Damned=== Over the span of three years, he used his fortune and intellect to gather a clandestine brotherhood of like-minded men and women. The brotherhood, which he called the Cult of the Damned, promised its acolytes social equality and eternal life on Azeroth in exchange for their service and obedience to Ner'zhul. As the months passed, Kel'Thuzad found many eager volunteers for his new cult amongst the tired, overburdened laborers of Lordaeron. Surprisingly, Kel'Thuzad's goal to pervert the citizens' faith in the Holy Light towards belief in Ner'zhul's dark shadow was easily attained. As the Cult of the Damned grew in size and influence, Kel'Thuzad made sure to keep its workings secret from the authorities of Lordaeron at every turn. On [[Caer Darrow]], Kel'Thuzad made a deal with the [[Barov]] family and some of his cultists moved into the [[Scholomance]].[[Eva Sarkhoff#Quotes]] With Kel'Thuzad's success in Lordaeron, the Lich King made the final preparations for his assault against human civilization. Placing his plague energies into a number of portable artifacts called plague cauldrons, Ner'zhul ordered Kel'Thuzad to transport the cauldrons to Lordaeron where they would be hidden within various cult-controlled villages. The cauldrons, protected by the loyal cultists, would then act as plague generators, sending the plague seeping out across the unsuspecting farmlands and cities of northern Lordaeron. The Lich King's plan worked perfectly. Many of Lordaeron's northern villages were contaminated almost immediately. Just as in Northrend, the citizens who contracted the plague died and arose as the Lich King's willing slaves. The cultists under Kel'Thuzad were eager to die and be raised again in their dark lord's service. They exulted in the prospect of immortality through undeath. As the plague spread, more and more feral zombies arose in the northlands. Kel'Thuzad looked upon the Lich King's growing army and named it the Scourge – for soon, it would march upon the gates of Lordaeron and scour humanity from the face of the world. ===The Scourge of Lordaeron=== Kel'Thuzad, upon the Lich King's instruction, oversaw the infection of the small town of [[Brill]], where he was discovered by [[Jaina Proudmoore]] and [[Prince Arthas]].[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Ravages_of_the_Plague_(WC3_Human) Ravages of the Plague (WC3 Human)] From there, he quickly fled, and they followed him back to [[Andorhal]], where he told Arthas of [[Mal'ganis]] in [[Stratholme]]. Arthas, in a rage, hunted Kel'Thuzad down and killed him. But they were not finished yet.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Cult_of_the_Damned_(WC3_Human) The Cult of the Damned (WC3_Human)] Kel'Thuzad waited patiently as a ghostly apparition until his protector, Gavinrad the Dire, was slain by a now-corrupted Arthas, and his remains were reclaimed. He appeared only to Arthas, and told him that he was not to trust the [[dreadlord]]s, promising to explain all of the Lich King's plans to Arthas once he walked the earth again in [[Quel'Thalas]].[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Digging_up_the_Dead_(WC3_Undead) Digging up the Dead (WC3 Undead)] Kel'Thuzad watched over Arthas as he made the slow procession to the [[Sunwell]] in [[Silvermoon]] against the stratagems of [[Sylvanas Windrunner]].[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Into_the_Realm_Eternal_(WC3_Undead) Into the Realm Eternal (WC3 Undead)] Eventually, Arthas ravaged his way through the two Elfgates[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Key_of_the_Three_Moons_(WC3_Undead) Key of the Three Moons (WC3 Undead)] and finally breached Silvermoon itself. With the help of [[Tichondrius]], Kel'Thuzad was reborn into the terrifying form of a [[lich]].[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Fall_of_Silvermoon_(WC3_Undead) The Fall of Silvermoon (WC3 Undead)] As they traveled to Alterac, Kel'Thuzad explained that the Scourge was merely the harbinger of the [[Burning Legion]], and that he would summon the first of the [[demon]]s, the [[Eredar]] warlock, [[Archimonde]], to the mortal world.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Revelation_(WC3_Undead) The Revelation (WC3 Undead)] After destroying the [[orc]]s guarding the Demon Gate, Kel'Thuzad communed with the dark lord, who told him that he must go to [[Dalaran]] and steal the [[Book of Medivh]] from Dalaran.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Blackrock_%26_Roll,_Too!_(WC3_Undead) Blackrock & Roll, Too! (WC3 Undead)] After Arthas led the attack on Dalaran and killed [[Antonidas]], the book was retrieved,[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Siege_of_Dalaran_(WC3_Undead) The Siege of Dalaran (WC3 Undead)] and Kel'Thuzad began the lengthy summoning process, with Arthas defending him from the many attacks of Dalaran and the [[Kirin Tor]]. Finally, all was complete, and Archimonde was set loose upon the world. His first act was to promote [[Tichondrius]] to leader of the Scourge, rendering Arthas and Kel'Thuzad of little use. However, Kel'Thuzad, confident in the Lich King's grand design, disappeared amidst the chaos of Dalaran's destruction.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Under_the_Burning_Sky_(WC3_Undead) Under the Burning Sky (WC3 Undead)] Kel'Thuzad resurfaced as the Legion raked across the Plaguelands, and in the aftermath of the invasion, he remained in the Capital City as one of the Lich King's lieutenants. Arthas had gone to Kalimdor on Ner'zhul's command to find the rogue demon hunter, Illidan, leaving only Kel'Thuzad and the banshee Sylvanas Windrunner remaining in his stead. However, both knew that the Legion was defeated long before the dreadlords who remained in Lordaeron did.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/King_Arthas_(WC3_Undead) King Arthas (WC3 Undead)] Arthas returned in a fury and chased the dreadlords out of the capital, and Kel'Thuzad was relieved to see him. With the Legion's generals gone, they turned to the human villages who were escaping to the mountain passes. Kel'Thuzad thought that perhaps they would be a fitting sacrifice to the Lich King and led his necromancers into battle against the paladin Magroth the Defender and his men protecting the human refugees. But as they cut a swath through the human forces, Arthas suffered some violent seizures, and Kel'Thuzad considered recalling their forces, but the King forbade it, and they continued on their macabre mission. In the aftermath, Arthas received a vision from Ner'zhul, who told him to return to Northrend. Kel'Thuzad immediately prepared for his departure, but they were abruptly ambushed by the dreadlords, and separated. The dreadlords unleashed their forces against Arthas, but Kel'Thuzad found his own way out of the city.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Flight_from_Lordaeron_(WC3_Undead) The Flight from Lordaeron (WC3 Undead)] Kel'Thuzad later came upon Arthas in the clutches of Sylvanas and her wicked banshees. She was about to strike when Kel'Thuzad unleashed his forces against her and her sisters. With the banshees dead, Sylvanas was forced to retreat. Kel'Thuzad escorted Arthas to the shore, where he had prepared a fleet of ships for his departure. Arthas asked Kel'Thuzad, as his most loyal servant and trusted friend, to remain in Lordaeron and ensure that his legacy endured. Kel'Thuzad swore on what was left of his life to carry out that mission at any cost.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Sylvanas%27_Farewell_(WC3_Undead) Sylvanas' Farewell (WC3 Undead)] While Sylvanas and her Forsaken claimed the Tirisfal Glades, Kel'Thuzad returned to the Eastern Plaguelands, which he ruled from the flying necropolis Naxxramas. ===Shadow of the Necropolis=== Kel'Thuzad began to seek out and reform [[Atiesh, Greatstaff of the Guardian]] - the very staff once held by [[Medivh]]. To this end, he had acquired the [[Staff Head of Atiesh]] and had already collected several of the staff's fragments - which were being held by his most trusted lieutenants.[[Archmage Angela Dosantos#Quotes]] As the Lich King stirred once more, Kel'Thuzad plotted the [[Scourge Invasion]] from the flying citadel of Naxxramas, leading to Scourge activity in the Plaguelands increasing ten-fold and attacks being reported as far away as [[Kalimdor]].[[Commander Eligor Dawnbringer#Quotes]] Kel'Thuzard amassing for another attack led to a coalition between the [[Argent Dawn]], the [[Scarlet Crusade]], the [[Cenarion Circle]], and the [[Earthen Ring]] to stop him. Ultimately, champions of the Argent Dawn ventured into Naxxramas and vanquished the lich. After his defeat, [[The Phylactery of Kel'Thuzad|his phylactery]] was delivered to [[Father Inigo Montoy]] at [[Light's Hope Chapel]]. ==References== {{reflist}} [[Category:Human characters]] [[Category:Liches]] [[Category:Mage characters]] [[Category:Kirin Tor]] [[Category:Dalaran (kingdom)]] [[Category:Cult of the Damned]] [[Category:Scourge]] [[Category:Deceased characters]]

The spire holds immense, uncontrolled power, with numerous factions vying to claim it as their own.https://turtle-wow.org/raids-and-dungeons ==History== ===The Last Guardian=== Karazhan is located in [[Deadwind Pass]] on the sub-continent of [[Azeroth (continent)|Azeroth]] in the [[Eastern Kingdoms]]. Existing long before [[Medivh]] inhabited it, it is unknown who originally built Karazhan or who now resides within its walls. The land it sits on "was similar in shape to a human skull. Many had noted it over the years, though only a few had been sufficiently brave, or powerful, or tactless to mention it to the property's owner". Karazhan's history begins with an explosion that carved out Deadwind Pass and weakened the fabric of reality in the region. Someone then built the tower, probably to take advantage of this weakened reality and heightened magic. Medivh eventually took up residence there, but mused that the explosion and the construction only happened because he would eventually arrive. During the [[First War]], the tower was inhabited by Medivh, his steward [[Moroes]], his cook named Cook, and his then-apprentice [[Khadgar]]. [[Garona]] also resided here as an emissary in the same time of Khadgar's apprenticeship. [[Sargeras]] allowed Medivh to freely explore Karazhan. As a result of the region's weakened reality, many strange and disturbing visions lurked within the tower, and Moroes was known for wearing blinders to avoid seeing them. The visions were ultimately ended when most of Karazhan's ambient magical power was absorbed by the resurrected Medivh, reducing it to "a pile of stone in the remote reaches", its power taken to serve the Prophet. ===World of Warcraft=== Despite Medivh's absence and the draining of magic, a new power seems to have made its home in Karazhan. The [[Dark Riders]] of [[Deadwind Pass]], though rarely seen, have a connection to Karazhan - the [[Dark Reaver of Karazhan]] standing vigil at the entrance of Karazhan, preventing any intrusion into his master's tower. However, no one knows who their master is. [[Jitters' Completed Journal|One recent sighting]] is cause for concern — the Dark Riders seek the [[Scythe of Elune]], a powerful artifact with the ability to summon the vile [[worgen]] into this world. In the depths of the lower halls, Medivh's loyal castellan, [[Moroes]], remains a vigilant guardian. The [[worgen]], led by [[Clawlord Howlfang]] and [[Keeper Gnarlmoon]], were summoned to the tower by the [[Scythe of Elune]], which has found itself through unknown means into the hands of [[Lord Blackwald II]], one of the [[Dark Riders]] cursed by Medivh himself to be artifact hunters.{{Neutral}} [60R] [[Scythe of the Goddess]]{{Neutral}} [60] [[Scythe of the Goddess (2)]] The worgen are further drawn to the tower seeking the Scythe up unknown means. Without the Last Guardian, the wild leylines that run beneath Karazhan stir with power, and have coalesced into an avatar of pure magic, taking form as [[Anomalus|a living force driven by vengeance]] that threatens to damage leylines across Azeroth and cause Karazhan to crumble to dust.[https://x.com/turtlewowteam/status/1819688372861907427 Turtle WoW Team on Twitter] (2024-08-03) The [[Blue dragonflight]], seeking to untangle the chaotic leylines, have also made themselves known in the tower led by [[Ley-Watcher Incantigos]]. Uncovering the mysteries of Karazhan's haunted upper halls unveils a terrifying truth - the evil of the [[Burning Legion]] still lingers in the haunted halls of Karazhan. == Objectives ==
Slay Keeper Krothis in Elun’aran and return to Sister Mirallun.
* [[Keeper Krothis]] slain

== Description ==
The druids behind this corruption do not act alone. Their leader is a keeper of the grove named Krothis.

Once he was respected among the druids of these lands. A guardian of the forest, patient and wise. Many sought his counsel when the wilds fell out of balance.

Now he serves another. The druids you fought speak of a figure they call Mothshroud.

Long ago, before many of these groves fell silent, an archdruid guided the druids of this region. A teacher of dreams, of night, of the hidden places between waking and the Emerald Dream. He walked paths few druids dared to study.

In time, those paths carried him somewhere… we could no longer follow. He vanished, and the groves slowly returned to simpler teachings.

But it seems his shadow has returned. Krothis now serves Mothshroud, carrying out his will across the groves.

If the forest is to heal, Krothis must fall.

== Progress ==
Krothis was once a keeper of the grove. Creatures like that do not fall easily and those who follow Mothshroud rarely fight alone.

== Completion ==
Krothis has fallen…

The forest mourns when a keeper dies, even one who lost his way.

Without Krothis guiding them, the corrupted druids will scatter. Some may yet remember the teachings they abandoned.

Others will follow Mothshroud deeper into shadow.

This is not the end of the matter. If Mothshroud truly walks these lands again, then the groves face a danger older than most remember.

But for now, the forest breathes a little easier.

You have done well.
